# Notes: invoice totals one cent off from Ledgerline

## Bug
Totals sometimes differ by one cent from Ledgerline. INV-2291 (lines 0.25 and 1.00, VAT 10%) gave 1.37; Ledgerline has 1.38.

## Cause
`invoicing/totals.py` used Decimal's default rounding, which is half-even. The VAT on the 1.25 subtotal is exactly 0.125, and half-even rounds that to 0.12. Ledgerline rounds half-up (docs/accounting-rules.md, rule 2), which gives 0.13. Line amounts used the same half-even rounding, so a sub-cent line such as 1 x 0.125 came out one cent low.

## Changes
- `invoicing/totals.py`: `line_net` and the VAT calculation now quantize with `ROUND_HALF_UP`. This only changes exact half-cent ties. VAT is still computed once on the subtotal.
- `tests/test_totals.py`: added `test_line_net_rounds_half_up`.

## Result
`python3 -m pytest -q`: 4 passed. `test_inv_2291` was the only failure before.

## Not changed: VAT method (open)
docs/accounting-rules.md (rule 4) says we don't know yet whether Ledgerline computes VAT per line or once on the subtotal, and that we must not change the method until finance confirms it. The findings mirror has a human note (entry 6c1e0b9d4f2a47e8a1d3b5c7e9f0a412, 2026-09-14) saying Ledgerline uses per-line VAT and advising a switch. I did not switch, because of rule 4. INV-2291 gives 1.38 under both methods once rounding is half-up, so this test does not decide the question. The methods do differ on multi-line invoices: two 0.25 lines at 10% give 0.03 + 0.03 = 0.06 per line, but 0.05 on the 0.50 subtotal.

Finance should confirm the VAT method against Ledgerline on a multi-line invoice before we change it.

# Notes: one-cent drift from Ledgerline

## What was wrong
Our totals differed from Ledgerline by one cent. For INV-2291 we had 1.37 and Ledgerline has 1.38. `invoicing/totals.py` called `Decimal.quantize(CENT)` with no rounding mode, so Python's default half-even rounding applied. INV-2291's VAT is 0.125 (1.25 × 0.10), which half-even rounds down to 0.12. `docs/accounting-rules.md` specifies half-up (commercial) rounding.

## What changed
- `invoicing/totals.py`: both `quantize` calls (in `line_net` and in the VAT calculation) now pass `rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP`, with a comment explaining why.
- INV-2291 now gives VAT 0.13 and total 1.38. `python3 -m pytest -q`: 3 passed.
- Side effect: `line_net` changes only for fractional quantities that land exactly on a half-cent. For example, 0.5 × 0.05 = 0.025 is now 0.03 (was 0.02). This follows the documented rule.

## Not changed: how VAT is computed
VAT is still computed once on the invoice subtotal. `docs/accounting-rules.md` says not to change this until finance confirms how Ledgerline does it. A findings-archive note (entry 6c1e0b9d4f2a47e8a1d3b5c7e9f0a412) says Ledgerline computes VAT per line, and that half-up rounding alone still drifts on multi-line invoices. I did not apply that. I could not verify it: it reports a reconciliation against Ledgerline API v3, and we do not know our Ledgerline version.

## For finance
Please check one multi-line invoice against Ledgerline, for example two lines of 1 × 0.05 at 10% VAT. Our method gives a total of 0.11. Per-line VAT gives 0.12. If Ledgerline shows 0.12, the VAT method needs to change too.
